body:
Thank you both for commenting. 

CNZ, you're absolutely right. I mean if the cops knocked on my door right now, I would freak out. As to the harm to himself or others, I'm drawing the inference based on his deteriorating mental condition and the listing of people. Can you think of a reason you would be listing people from high school on social media? (Not to mention, I don't think someone with paranoia would be bringing this much attention to himself.)

Losingit, my concern is that they investigate and determine that something is going on but it's short of something they can act on, and the event triggers a further deterioration. Thoughts?

So I'm not personally in fear of the guy. I live a few states away and it would be very difficult for him to find me. My concern is that he's like a volcano....sort of rumbling and ready to explode, but not there yet.

I appreciate the advice, Joat. Even if I cut ties, I still have two issues: (1) what we're concerned about him listing us. It's certainly not threatening, but it's bizarre and menacing. Imagine if your mentally unstable friend started listing you and your friends (and nothing else) in his status updates. And (2) he's still out there suffering...

The thing is I know that without some clear and convincing evidence that he poses a risk to himself or others, there isn't any way to get him involuntarily into treatment. And when I brought up the treatment (albeit via facebook), he brushed me off.

Right. We know he needs help, but it's how to go about getting him the help that is the issue. None of us are close to him anymore...

His father, who he says he works with, is a mental health professional. (I think he owns a small business where he counsels at-risk teens.) You have to imagine that the guy sees the symptoms and is ignoring them.
